name: Left acetabular posterior column fragment
note: A displaced fragment of the posterior column of the left acetabulum, part of a comminuted fracture.

name: Left acetabular anterior column fragment
note: A fragment of the anterior column of the left acetabulum, displaced from the socket rim.

name: Left acetabular comminuted fragments
note: Several small loose bone fragments in the left acetabulum, the comminution the source describes.

name: Left acetabular fracture line
note: The fracture line crossing the left acetabulum from the posterior column to the anterior column.

name: Right renal calculus
note: A small dense calculus in the lower, medial part of the right kidney; it is bright on non-contrast CT.

name: Left renal calculus
note: A small dense calculus in the left kidney, near the renal pelvis; it is bright on non-contrast CT.

name: Left subdural haematoma (convexity)
note: Acute blood lying as a crescent between the left cerebral convexity and the inner table of the skull, the thicker collection on this scan.

name: Right subdural haematoma (convexity)
note: A thinner crescent of acute blood between the right frontoparietal convexity and the skull, the second collection on this scan.

name: Right proximal ureteric stone
note: A calculus lodged in the right proximal ureter just below the renal pelvis, the obstructing stone described in the source.

name: Saddle pulmonary embolus
note: A saddle clot sits across the pulmonary arterial bifurcation and extends into both pulmonary arteries.

name: Left lobar pulmonary embolus
note: Clot extending from the bifurcation into the left pulmonary artery.

name: Right lobar pulmonary embolus
note: Clot extending from the bifurcation into the right pulmonary artery.

name: T10 Chance fracture
note: A horizontal (Chance) fracture runs through the T10 vertebral body and posterior elements after a seatbelt injury in a motor vehicle collision.

name: T9 vertebral body fracture
note: An associated fracture through the T9 vertebral body from the same seatbelt injury.

name: Aortic dissection flap
note: The intimal flap splitting the descending thoracic aorta into a true and a false lumen, as in a Stanford type B dissection.

name: Transverse myelitis central cord hyperintensity
note: Increased central T2 signal in a segment of the cervical cord, the MRI sign of transverse myelitis (inflammation across the cord).

name: Gallbladder stones
note: Multiple gallstones in the gallbladder, seen as filling defects in the fluid-filled gallbladder on MRCP.

name: Common bile duct stone
note: A stone lodged in the common bile duct, causing a filling defect in the otherwise fluid-filled duct on MRCP.

name: Dilated left ventricle
note: The left ventricular cavity is enlarged and rounded, as in the left image. This shows chamber size only; contractility and ejection fraction are not reported.

name: Left basal ganglia infarct
note: Hyperacute left basal ganglia infarction: restricted diffusion, bright on DWI and low on ADC four hours after onset. Conventional T2 did not show it clearly.

name: L4-L5 left paramedian disc herniation
note: Posterior herniation of the L4–L5 disc, left paramedian, indenting the thecal sac and the emerging left L5 root sheath.

name: Uterine fibroid (illustrative)
note: Well-circumscribed uterine fibroid (leiomyoma) in the central pelvis, shown illustratively. The atlas has no uterus, so its position is approximate.

name: Second uterine fibroid (illustrative)
note: Second uterine fibroid in the central pelvis, shown illustratively next to the first.

name: Right frontal cortical infarct
note: Subacute cortical infarct of the right frontal lobe: restricted diffusion on DWI with gadolinium enhancement of the cortex on enhanced T1 from blood-brain-barrier disruption.

name: Supraspinatus tendon tear
note: Complete full-thickness tear of the supraspinatus tendon, about 2.4 cm wide, with the gap filled by fluid.

name: Left basal ganglia infarct (mri_hyperacute_basal_ganglia_infarct_adc)
note: Hyperacute infarction of the left basal ganglia: restricted diffusion with low ADC, bright on the paired DWI.

name: Right medial thalamic FLAIR signal abnormality
note: Hyperintense FLAIR signal in the right mesial dorsal thalamus, the abnormality described in Wernicke encephalopathy (oedema or gliosis; illustrative marker, not registered to this scan).

name: Left medial thalamic FLAIR signal abnormality
note: Hyperintense FLAIR signal in the left mesial dorsal thalamus, the abnormality described in Wernicke encephalopathy (oedema or gliosis; illustrative marker, not registered to this scan).

name: Dilated oesophagus in achalasia
note: The lower oesophageal sphincter fails to relax, so the oesophagus dilates above it and fills with retained barium and food.

name: Killian-Jamieson diverticulum
note: A small lateral outpouching of the cervical oesophagus just below the cricopharyngeus, retaining contrast on the barium swallow.

name: Cerebral arterial aneurysm
note: A rounded saccular outpouching of an intracranial artery on catheter angiography, with the sac filled by contrast.

name: Left renal artery bead 1
note: Fibromuscular dysplasia of the lower accessory left renal artery: one bead of the string-of-beads wall contour.

name: Left renal artery bead 2
note: Fibromuscular dysplasia of the lower accessory left renal artery: a second bead of the string-of-beads wall contour.

name: Left renal artery bead 3
note: Fibromuscular dysplasia of the lower accessory left renal artery: a third bead of the string-of-beads wall contour.

name: Right renal artery distal aneurysm
note: A small saccular aneurysm of the distal right renal artery, as described in the source image.

name: Posterior tibial artery occlusion
note: A clot fills the posterior tibial artery from its origin to the ankle, so it is not opacified on the angiogram.

name: Collateral vessels around the occlusion
note: Small collateral channels bridge from the posterior tibial artery to the fibular artery and carry blood around the occlusion.

name: Proximal femoral occlusion
note: A thrombus fills the upper femoral artery, so contrast does not pass beyond it.

name: Distal popliteal occlusion
note: A thrombus at the popliteal artery blocks flow to the leg below the knee.

name: Left subcapital insufficiency fracture
note: Focal tracer uptake at the left subcapital femoral neck, the insufficiency fracture the bone scan shows.

name: Hodgkin paratracheal nodal mass
note: FDG-avid enlarged mediastinal lymph node mass to the right of the trachea, typical of Hodgkin lymphoma. Shown as an illustrative mass; the 3D atlas is not registered to this scan.

name: Left ICA complete occlusion
note: Thrombus filling the left internal carotid artery, giving the complete occlusion described by the source; the clot is illustrative and is not seen directly on the B-mode image.

name: Common carotid intimal flap (dissection)
note: A thin intimal flap lies within the common carotid artery and separates two lumen channels. The source does not state the side or which channel is the true lumen; the left side is shown for illustration only.

name: Left ICA near-occlusion plaque
note: Atheromatous plaque narrowing the left internal carotid artery lumen to near occlusion, with only residual flow.

name: Hydronephrosis (dilated renal pelvis)
note: Obstructed urine backs up and dilates the renal pelvis and calyces, shown here as an anechoic collecting system on ultrasound.

name: Gallstones (dependent, shadowing)
note: Echogenic gallstones lying in the dependent part of the gallbladder, producing posterior acoustic shadowing.

name: Biliary sludge (dependent layer)
note: Mixed echoes of biliary sludge layering in the dependent gallbladder lumen beneath the stones.

name: Impacted gallstone
note: A stone of about 1.9 cm impacted at the gallbladder neck, the cause of the acoustic shadow behind it on ultrasound.

name: Gallbladder wall thickening
note: Thickened gallbladder wall (about 4 mm) from acute inflammation, as reported with the cholecystitis.

name: Hashimoto thyroiditis enlarged right lobe
note: Diffuse lymphocytic inflammation enlarges and darkens the right thyroid lobe on ultrasound; the lobe is hypoechoic and heterogeneous.

name: Femoral vein thrombus
note: Thrombus filling the femoral vein; the vein lacks colour flow on Doppler, while the femoral artery and deep femoral vein fill with colour.

name: Abdominal aortic aneurysm
note: Focal dilatation of the infrarenal-to-suprarenal abdominal aorta seen in transverse section; the image shows enlargement without a calibrated diameter.

name: Baker's cyst fluid
note: A fluid collection in the popliteal fossa between the semimembranosus tendon and the medial head of gastrocnemius, seen as an elongated anechoic cyst on longitudinal ultrasound.

name: Dilated small bowel with air-fluid levels
note: Distended small bowel loops hold fluid with gas above, giving horizontal air-fluid levels on the upright film. A single projection does not show the transition point.

name: L3 compression fracture
note: Anterior-superior wedge collapse of the L3 vertebral body with reduced height and depression of the upper endplate.

name: Distal radius fracture
note: Transverse fracture through the distal radial metaphysis with the distal fragment displaced dorsally (Colles pattern).

name: Dorsally displaced radial fragment
note: Distal radial fragment displaced dorsally at the Colles fracture site.

name: Ulnar styloid fracture
note: Fracture of the ulnar styloid process at the distal ulna, with a small separated tip fragment.

name: Clavicular fracture
note: Transverse fracture of the mid-shaft of the left clavicle with separated fragments.

name: Calcaneal fracture line
note: Fracture line through the body of the calcaneus, seen as a disrupted heel-bone contour on the lateral radiograph.

name: Right renal calculus (xr_bilateral_renal_stones)
note: Radiopaque renal calculus in the right kidney, visible on the frontal abdominal radiograph.

name: Left renal calculus (xr_bilateral_renal_stones)
note: Radiopaque renal calculus in the left kidney, visible on the frontal abdominal radiograph.

name: Dilated upper lobe vessels
note: Upper-lobe arteries and veins are equal to or wider than the lower-lobe ones: blood diverted to the upper zones as pulmonary venous pressure rises.

structures: Apical segmental artery of right lung
Anterior segmental artery of right lung
